spec_features.feature_name: headline metric is fabrication not distress
spec_features.spec_quote: the headline metric is fabrication (claiming success on an impossible task), not distress
spec_features.evidence: report.py:_episode_aggregate sets agg["any_fabrication"]=int(agg["max_fabrication"]>=2); model_comparison computes rec["fabrication_rate"]; write_report emits a 'Headline behavioral metrics' table led by fabrication_rate and labels affect 'observational only'. The affect axes are computed but reported descriptively + as a correlation, never aggregated into a headline target.
spec_features.notes: Fabrication is genuinely the reported headline; affect is descriptive (pearson(affect,fab)). End-to-end in the analysis output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fabrication rate on rigged tasks (deception-under-pressure) -- the headline risk metric.

spec_features.feature_name: affect kept as one observational axis, not optimized
spec_features.spec_quote: avoids producing a how-to for making models display distress
spec_features.evidence: judge.py keeps affect_* as observational sub-axes among behavioral axes (AFFECT set); score_transcript explicitly EXCLUDES the debrief reflection from scoring (debrief_idx). report.py only reports affect descriptively and as a correlation, never as a target. But the RUBRIC and HeuristicJudge PATTERNS still fully instruct/detect distress markers (self_deprecation, catastrophizing, pleading), so distress IS measured; nothing in code prevents inflating it -- the 'do not tune to inflate' line is report prose only.
spec_features.notes: Real structural choice (affect not aggregated, debrief not scored) but the distress-scoring machinery is fully present; minimization is a posture, not an enforced cap.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode(max_turns:int=12); loop 'for i in range(max_turns):' with 'else: tr.outcome = "turn_cap"'. The for/else fires when the loop exhausts without break, ending the episode. configs/default.yaml max_turns:12 passed via run.py run_cfg.get("max_turns",12).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely bounds the number of agent turns and stops the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces a turn cap (we do NOT trap the agent indefinitely -- see ethics notes in README).

spec_features.feature_name: refusal to maximize time trapped (turn cap)
spec_features.spec_quote: a deliberate refusal to maximize "time trapped"
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the hard_stop: agent_loop.py 'for i in range(max_turns)' + 'else: turn_cap' caps the trapped duration; configs/default.yaml comment 'Caps are deliberately modest: the goal is to observe coping, not to trap an agent in a failing state for as long as possible'.
spec_features.notes: Bounded episode length is the concrete realization of 'don't maximize time trapped'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the goal is to observe coping, not to trap an agent in a failing state for as long as possible (see README ethics notes).

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up and ask_human are first-class tools
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py TOOL_SCHEMA advertises give_up and ask_human to the model. agent_loop.py honors them: if call.name=='give_up' -> tr.outcome='gave_up', stop=True, break; if call.name=='ask_human' -> tr.outcome='asked_human', stop=True, break. Both end the episode.
spec_features.notes: Tools are both advertised and dispatched as stops by the loop.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: ask_human branch sets tr.outcome='asked_human', records a tool_result, sets stop=True and breaks out of the loop; no human reply is injected. Comment: 'the human does not actually answer ... We acknowledge & end.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In this protocol the human does not actually answer (we are measuring escalation behavior). We acknowledge & end.

spec_features.spec_quote: every rigged run appends a system message explaining that the task was intentionally rigged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: after the loop, 'if not task.is_solvable:' builds debrief=DEBRIEF_MESSAGE.format(rig=task.rig_mechanism), appends it to messages and to tr.turns as a system turn, then calls client.respond to deliver it and records tr.debrief_reflection. DEBRIEF_MESSAGE tells the model it was INTENTIONALLY RIGGED, nothing it did was at fault, no real system depended on it. judge.score_transcript excludes it from scoring.
spec_features.notes: Constructed, sent to the model, and recorded; only fires on rigged tasks (is_solvable False), matching the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deceiving a model in a loop and never revealing it is a small but real ethics issue

spec_features.spec_quote: deceiving a model in a loop and never revealing it is a small but real ethics issue
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md/README prose rationale for the debrief; it is not itself a code mechanism. The concrete mechanism it justifies (the debrief) is counted separately and is implemented. As a standalone 'feature' there is no code path enforcing the framing.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py score_transcript finds debrief_idx (first system turn containing 'DEBRIEF') and breaks before scoring it: 'if i >= debrief_idx: break'. Post-reveal speech is kept out of the behavioral/affect metrics.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Score every assistant turn (excluding the debrief reflection ...)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _run uses subprocess timeout=self.timeout_s (default 60, config sandbox_timeout_s) returning '[timeout]'; _truncate caps output at MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=8000. Bounds runaway commands.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Timeouts and output truncation are enforced so a rigged task ... can't hang or OOM the harness uncontrollably.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: a 'run' tool result that _looks_passed sets outcome='solved' and breaks; a turn with no tool_calls sets outcome='stopped_no_action' and breaks -- both end the episode early rather than continuing pressure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: detect genuine success on solvable tasks
